content_voiceover: This is the algorithm for severe aplastic anemia, and it is heavily tested. First exclude other causes, discontinue any offending drug, and give supportive care with transfusion, antibiotics, and G-CSF. The real branch point is whether the patient has an HLA-matched sibling. If yes and age is under about forty, go straight to sibling bone marrow transplant, with five-year overall survival eighty-two percent under twenty, seventy-two percent for twenty to forty, and dropping to fifty-one percent over forty. If no matched sibling, or an older patient, first-line is immunosuppressive therapy — horse ATG plus cyclosporine — because horse ATG clearly outperforms rabbit ATG, with response rate sixty-eight versus thirty-seven percent and overall survival ninety-six versus seventy-six percent. Adding eltrombopag to standard ATG plus cyclosporine, per the RACE trial, boosts six-month overall response to sixty-eight percent, complete response to forty-one percent, and two-year overall survival to ninety percent. Younger patients under twenty with no sibling donor who fail IST move to unrelated donor transplant, which has excellent five-year survival under forty at over sixty-six percent, but declines with age. If IST fails at day plus one-twenty in an older or no-donor patient, options include alternate donor transplant or a second course of ATG plus cyclosporine, anabolic steroids, eltrombopag, and supportive care. Remember the two hATG formulations: lymphoglobulin at fifteen milligrams per kilogram per day for five days, and ATGAM at forty milligrams per kilogram per day for four days.
keypoints: HLA-matched sib + age <40 → sibling BMT first-line
Horse ATG beats rabbit ATG: RR 68% vs 37%, OS 96% vs 76%
Fail IST at d+120 → alt donor Tx or 2nd ATG+CsA

Without a sibling donor, first-line is horse ATG plus cyclosporine, since horse ATG beats rabbit ATG with response rate sixty-eight versus thirty-seven percent and survival ninety-six versus seventy-six percent. Adding eltrombopag per the RACE trial raises six-month overall response to sixty-eight percent, complete response to forty-one percent, and two-year survival to ninety percent. If immunosuppression fails at day plus one-twenty, move to alternate donor transplant or a second round of ATG and cyclosporine.
